Refuse to modify a user with a higher role (#1132)

* Refuse to modify a user with a higher role

An owner could edit, demote or delete a site admin in their tree, since
the user endpoints only checked the caller's permissions, not the
target's role. In a single-tree setup, the first user is a site admin
and shares the tree with any owners. By changing the admin's e-mail
address and triggering a password reset, an owner could take over the
admin account.

Editing another user, changing their password and deleting them now
answer 403 if the user has a higher role than the caller. Users with
the same role can still act on each other, so co-owners can manage
each other.

* Look up both roles by user ID and refuse unknown users

The role check looked up the caller's name by ID and then their role by
name, and let the request through if either user could not be found. A
caller renaming themselves concurrently could make the second lookup
miss and skip the check. Both roles are now looked up by ID, which
cannot change, and a user that cannot be found is +def abort_if_higher_role(user_id: str) -> None:
+    """Abort if the user has a higher role than the user making the request.
+
+    Otherwise an owner could, for instance, change a site admin's e-mail
+    address and take over the account with a password reset.
+
+    Both users are looked up by GUID, since a name can change concurrently,
+    and a user that cannot be found is refused.
+    """
+    try:
+        role = get_role(str(user_id))
+        own_role = get_role(get_jwt_identity())
+    except ValueError:
+        abort_with_message(403, "Not allowed to modify a user with a higher role")
+    if role > own_role:
+        abort_with_message(403, "Not allowed to modify a user with a higher role")
+

+def get_role(guid: str) -> int:
+    """Get the role of an existing user by GUID."""
+    try:
+        query = user_db.session.query(User.role)  # pylint: disable=no-member
+        role = query.filter_by(id=guid).scalar()
+    except StatementError as exc:
+        raise ValueError(f"User ID {guid} not found") from exc
+    if role is None:
+        raise ValueError(f"User ID {guid} not found")
+    return role

+    def test_edit_higher_role_forbidden(self):
+        """An owner may not edit, demote or delete a site admin in their tree."""
+        # "owner" and "admin" both belong to self.tree
+        rv = self.client.post(
+            BASE_URL + "/token/",
+            json={"username": "owner", "password": "123"},
+        )
+        assert rv.status_code == 200
+        token_owner = rv.json["access_token"]
+        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {token_owner}"}
+        # changing the e-mail address would allow a takeover by password reset
+        rv = self.client.put(
+            BASE_URL + "/users/admin/",
+            headers=headers,
+            json={"email": "takeover@example.com"},
+        )
+        assert rv.status_code == 403
+        rv = self.client.put(
+            BASE_URL + "/users/admin/", headers=headers, json={"role": ROLE_DISABLED}
+        )
+        assert rv.status_code == 403
+        rv = self.client.post(
+            BASE_URL + "/users/admin/password/change",
+            headers=headers,
+            json={"old_password": "123", "new_password": "456"},
+        )
+        assert rv.status_code == 403
+        rv = self.client.delete(BASE_URL + "/users/admin/", headers=headers)
+        assert rv.status_code == 403
+        details = get_user_details("admin")
+        assert details["email"] == "admin@example.com"
+        assert details["role"] == ROLE_ADMIN
+
+    def test_edit_by_unknown_caller_forbidden(self):
+        """A caller whose own user cannot be found is refused, not let through."""

+            add_user(name="owner3", password="123", role=ROLE_OWNER, tree=self.tree)
+        rv = self.client.post(
+            BASE_URL + "/token/",
+            json={"username": "owner3", "password": "123"},
+        )
+        assert rv.status_code == 200
+        token_owner = rv.json["access_token"]
+        with self.app.app_context():
+            delete_user("owner3")
+        rv = self.client.put(
+            BASE_URL + "/users/admin/",
+            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token_owner}"},
+            json={"email": "takeover@example.com"},
+        )
+        assert rv.status_code == 403
+        assert get_user_details("admin")["email"] == "admin@example.com"
+
